Need to search first.I don't have any commentary notes on Isaiah 58 for you yet, because I couldn't read any sources this session.

My first try was to open the commentary pages directly (Enduring Word, BibleHub, Precept Austin, NET Bible notes, StudyLight). Each one was refused because the system only lets me open pages that a search has already returned. I then ran the searches, covering the main Isaiah 58 commentaries, the Sabbath verse (v. 13), Gill, Ellicott, the NET Bible notes, Catholic views on fasting, Spurgeon and Desiring God. But I had used up my tool calls for this turn, so no results came back. That means I haven't read a single page.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, with a link for each point, and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written anything: any verse notes now would come from memory, not from sources.

If you reply (even just "continue"), I'll start again with fresh tool access. I would:
1. Run the searches first, then open the pages they return: Enduring Word, the BibleHub/StudyLight entries for Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary, Precept Austin, and the NET Bible notes.
2. Look for differences between Protestant traditions where they're likely to show up. That's mainly v. 13–14 (whether and how the Sabbath applies to Christians), plus v. 6–7 (how good works relate to faith).
3. Check the Catholic and Orthodox sites for their reading of fasting in v. 3–7. I'd also look for any prosperity-style use of v. 8–12 and 14 ("ride on the heights," "well-watered garden").

Then I'll write the notes verse by verse, with a link after each point, and leave out anything I can't find.
